    Ichimoku cloud

    Ichimoku is an indicator of five lines that shows the trend's direction, its pace and where price sits against past ranges on one chart. Its best-known part is the cloud, the fill between two lines, which is drawn 26 candles ahead. The common setting is 9/26/52. None of the lines is an average; each is the middle of a period's highest and lowest price.

    Which question does Ichimoku answer?

    Ichimoku answers this question: where is price relative to the short, medium and long-term ranges? Each line is the middle of a period's highest and lowest price: over 9, 26 and 52 candles. Price above or below these middles shows which half of that period's range it is in.

    That is where the name, "one-glance equilibrium chart", comes from: it gathers several time scales in one view. The cost is a busy chart, so it matters to know each line on its own.

    How the five lines are calculated

    1. Tenkan-sen (conversion line). The middle of the last 9 candles' highest and lowest price: (highest + lowest) ÷ 2. The short-term balance.
    2. Kijun-sen (base line). The same over the last 26 candles. The medium-term balance; it moves more slowly than Tenkan.
    3. Senkou Span A. (Tenkan + Kijun) ÷ 2, drawn 26 candles ahead of the candle it is calculated on.
    4. Senkou Span B. The middle of the last 52 candles' highest and lowest price, also drawn 26 candles ahead. The area between Span A and Span B is the cloud.
    5. Chikou Span (lagging line). The candle's close, drawn 26 candles back. It lines today's close up with the price 26 candles ago.

    How it is commonly read

    • Price above or below the cloud: price is above or below the medium and long-term balances calculated 26 candles ago. Inside the cloud reads as the undecided area between the two balances.
    • The cloud's colour: green while Span A is above Span B, red while it is below. It shows where the average of the short and medium-term balances sits against the long-term middle.
    • Tenkan and Kijun: Tenkan above Kijun says the last 9 candles' range sits higher than the last 26 candles'. Their cross describes a change in the short-term balance.
    • Chikou: today's close above or below the price 26 candles ago shows whether price rose or fell over that span.
    • Cloud thickness: as Span A and B move apart the cloud thickens; the periods differ a lot. A thin cloud shows the periods' balances are close together.

    Ichimoku was first designed for markets with a six-day trading week; the numbers 9, 26 and 52 come from that calendar. Crypto trades 24/7, so some users pick other settings; the common setting is used here.

    Same cloud, different market

    How Ichimoku reads depends on the structure of the market.

    Clear trend

    Price stays on one side of the cloud for a long time, Tenkan and Kijun keep the same order, and the cloud thickens in one colour.

    Sideways market

    Price moves in and out of the cloud, Tenkan and Kijun cross often, and the cloud thins and changes colour.

    A sharp move

    One sharp move carries Tenkan quickly, but Kijun and Span B react more slowly; the lines drift apart for a while.

    What it shows, what it does not prove

    What it shows

    • Where price sits against the middles of the 9, 26 and 52-candle ranges
    • The order of the short, medium and long-term balances
    • Where the cloud sits 26 candles ahead, drawn from today's data

    What it does not prove

    • Where price will be relative to the cloud; the cloud drawn ahead is not a forecast, it is today's data shifted forward
    • That the cloud will hold as support or resistance
    • Direction on its own; all the lines come from past prices

    The MarketLevelMap view

    How it relates to zones

    The cloud's edges are calculated from the middles of past ranges; they are not the same as areas where the market has reacted before. Still, from which side of the cloud price approaches a support or resistance zone gives context.

    A zone that falls in the same price range as a cloud edge shows two separate calculations pointing at the same place. The two observations are not independent and give no certainty; reading them together only enriches the description.

    Ichimoku in crypto

    Crypto has no weekend or overnight gaps, so 9/26/52 candles cover a different stretch of the calendar than in traditional markets. On the daily chart, for example, 26 candles are exactly 26 calendar days, not about a month of trading days.

    Often confused with

    • Moving averages (SMA, EMA)Moving averages are averages of closes; Ichimoku lines are the middle of a period's highest and lowest price, so they can stay flat in quiet periods.
    • SupertrendBoth describe the trend's direction. Supertrend is a single trailing line; Ichimoku shows several periods and a cloud drawn ahead together.

    Key points

    • Ichimoku lines are the middles of a period's highest and lowest price: 9 (Tenkan), 26 (Kijun), 52 (Span B).
    • The cloud is the area between Span A and Span B, drawn 26 candles ahead.
    • Chikou is the close drawn 26 candles back.
    • The cloud drawn ahead is not a forecast; it is today's data shifted forward.
